name: Real
fourierIntegral_convergent_iff
result.signature: {μ : Measure V} {f : V → E} (w : V) : Integrable (fun v : V ↦ 𝐞 (-⟪v, w⟫) • f v) μ ↔ Integrable f μ
result.informal_name: Fourier Integral Convergent iff Function Integrable
result.informal_description: For a measure $\mu$ on a space $V$, a function $f : V \to E$ taking values in a normed space $E$, and an element $w \in V$, the function $v \mapsto e^{-2\pi i \langle v, w \rangle} \cdot f(v)$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$ if and only if $f$ itself is integrable with respect to $\mu$. Here, $e^{-2\pi i \langle v, w \rangle}$ denotes the Fourier character applied to the pairing $\langle v, w \rangle$ between elements of $V$.

name: tsum_sq_fourierCoeffOn
result.signature:
{a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b) (hL2 : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc a b))) :
  ∑' (i : ℤ), ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f i‖ ^ 2 = (b - a)⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, ‖f x‖ ^ 2
result.type:
∀ {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b),
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b)) →
    ∑' (i : ℤ), ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f i‖ ^ 2 = (b - a)⁻¹ • ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, ‖f x‖ ^ 2
result.informal_name: Parseval's Identity for Fourier Coefficients on an Interval
result.informal_description: For real numbers $a < b$ and a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is square-integrable on $(a, b]$, the sum of the squared moduli of its Fourier coefficients equals $\frac{1}{b - a}$ times the integral of $|f(x)|^2$ over $[a, b]$. Formally, $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} |c_n|^2 = \frac{1}{b - a} \int_{a}^{b} |f(x)|^2 \, dx$, where $c_n$ denotes the $n$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $(a, b]$.

name: hasSum_sq_fourierCoeffOn
result.signature:
{a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b) (hL2 : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc a b))) :
  HasSum (fun i => ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f i‖ ^ 2) ((b - a)⁻¹ • ∫ x in a..b, ‖f x‖ ^ 2)
result.type:
∀ {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hab : a < b),
  MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc a b)) →
    HasSum (fun i => ‖fourierCoeffOn hab f i‖ ^ 2) ((b - a)⁻¹ • ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, ‖f x‖ ^ 2)
result.value:
:= by
  haveI := Fact.mk (by linarith : 0 < b - a)
  rw [← add_sub_cancel a b] at hL2
  have h := hL2.memLp_liftIoc.haarAddCircle
  convert hasSum_sq_fourierCoeff h.toLp using 1
  · simp [fourierCoeff_congr_ae h.coeFn_toLp, fourierCoeff_liftIoc_eq]
  · nth_rw 2 [← add_sub_cancel a b]
    rw [← AddCircle.integral_liftIoc_eq_intervalIntegral, ← Function.comp_def (f := (‖·‖ ^ 2))]
    simp only [liftIoc_comp_apply, ← AddCircle.integral_haarAddCircle]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upward...
result.informal_name: Parseval's Identity for Fourier Coefficients on an Interval
result.informal_description: For real numbers $a < b$ and a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ in $L^2$ on $(a, b]$, the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ over $(a, b]$ equals $\frac{1}{b - a}$ times the integral of $|f(x)|^2$ over $[a, b]$. Specifically, $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \left\|\int_{t \in (a,b]} e^{-i \frac{2\pi n}{b-a}(t - a)} f(t)\, dt\right\|^2 = \frac{1}{b - a} \int_{a}^{b} |f(x)|^2 \, dx$.

name: UnitAddTorus
hasSum_prod_mFourierCoeff
result.signature: (f g : L²(UnitAddTorus d)) : HasSum (fun i ↦ conj (mFourierCoeff f i) * (mFourierCoeff g i)) (∫ t, conj (f t) * g t)
result.type:
∀ {d : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype d] (f g : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 MeasureTheory.volume)),
  HasSum (fun i => (starRingEnd ℂ) (UnitAddTorus.mFourierCoeff (↑↑f) i) * UnitAddTorus.mFourierCoeff (↑↑g) i)
    (∫ (t : UnitAddTorus d), (starRingEnd ℂ) (↑↑f t) * ↑↑g t)
result.value:
:= by
  simp_rw [mul_comm (conj _)]
  refine HasSum.congr_fun (mFourierBasis.hasSum_inner_mul_inner f g) (fun n ↦ ?_)
  simp only [← mFourierBasis_repr, HilbertBasis.repr_apply_apply, inner_conj_symm, mul_comm (inner ℂ f _)]
result.informal_name: Parseval's Identity for Fourier Coefficients on the Additive Torus
result.informal_description: For any square-integrable functions $f, g$ on the $d$-dimensional additive torus $\mathbb{R}^d/\mathbb{Z}^d$, the sum over all indices $i$ of the product of the complex conjugate of the $i$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$ and the $i$-th Fourier coefficient of $g$ converges to the inner product $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d/\mathbb{Z}^d} \overline{f(t)} g(t) \, dt$.

name: hasSum_fourier_series_of_summable
result.signature: (h : Summable (fourierCoeff f)) : HasSum (fun i => fourierCoeff f i • fourier i) f
result.type:
∀ {T : ℝ} [hT : Fact (0 < T)] {f : C(AddCircle T, ℂ)},
  Summable (fourierCoeff ⇑f) → HasSum (fun i => fourierCoeff (⇑f) i • fourier i) f
result.value:
:= by
  have sum_L2 := hasSum_fourier_series_L2 (toLp (E := ℂ) 2 haarAddCircle ℂ f)
  simp_rw [fourierCoeff_toLp] at sum_L2
  refine ContinuousMap.hasSum_of_hasSum_Lp (.of_norm ?_) sum_L2
  simp_rw [norm_smul, fourier_norm, mul_one]
  exact h.norm
result.informal_name: Fourier Series Convergence: Summable Coefficients Imply $\sum c_n e_n = f$
result.informal_description: If the Fourier coefficients of a function $ f $ are summable, then the Fourier series $\sum_{n} c_n e_n $, where $ c_n $ denotes the $ n $-th Fourier coefficient of $ f $ and $ e_n $ is the $ n $-th Fourier character, converges to $ f $.

name: Complex
mem_rootsOfUnity
result.signature: (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (x : Units ℂ) : x ∈ rootsOfUnity n ℂ ↔ ∃ i < n, exp (2 * π * I * (i / n)) = x
result.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (x : ℂˣ), x ∈ rootsOfUnity n ℂ ↔ ∃ i < n, Complex.exp (2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * (↑i / ↑n)) = ↑x
result.value:
:= by
  rw [mem_rootsOfUnity, Units.ext_iff, Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val, Units.val_one]
  have hn0 : (n : ℂ) ≠ 0 := mod_cast NeZero.out
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨i, hi, H⟩ : ∃ i < (n : ℕ), exp (2 * π * I / n) ^ i = x := by
      simpa only using (isPrimitiveRoot_exp n NeZero.out).eq_pow_of_pow_eq_one h
    refine ⟨i, hi, ?_⟩
    rw [← H, ← exp_nat_mul]
    congr 1
    ring
  · rintro ⟨i, _, H⟩
    rw [← H, ← exp_nat_mul, exp_eq_one_iff]
    use i
    simp [field]
result.informal_name: Membership in the n-th Roots of Unity Subgroup of Complex Numbers
result.informal_description: For any non-zero natural number $ n $ and any invertible complex number $ x $, $ x $ is an $ n $-th root of unity if and only if there exists an integer $ k $ less than $ n $ such that $ x = e^{2\pi i k/n} $.

name: IsPrimitiveRoot
geom_sum_eq_zero
result.signature: [IsDomain R] {ζ : R} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k) (hk : 1 < k) : ∑ i ∈ range k, ζ ^ i = 0
result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_4} {k : ℕ} [inst : CommRing R] [IsDomain R] {ζ : R},
  IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k → 1 < k → ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ζ ^ i = 0
result.value:
:= by
  refine eq_zero_of_ne_zero_of_mul_left_eq_zero (sub_ne_zero_of_ne (hζ.ne_one hk).symm) ?_
  rw [mul_neg_geom_sum, hζ.pow_eq_one, sub_self]
result.informal_name: Geometric Sum Identity for Primitive Roots of Unity
result.informal_description: In an integral domain $ R $, if $ \zeta $ is a primitive $ k $-th root of unity and $ k > 1 $, then the sum $ \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \zeta^i = 0 $. This identity holds because the minimal polynomial of a primitive $ k $-th root of unity over a domain has coefficients summing to zero.

name: Complex
isPrimitiveRoot_exp
result.signature: (n : ℕ) (h0 : n ≠ 0) : IsPrimitiveRoot (exp (2 * π * I / n)) n
result.value: := by simpa only [Nat.cast_one, one_div] using isPrimitiveRoot_exp_of_coprime 1 n h0 n.coprime_one_left
result.informal_name: e^{2\pi i/n} is a Primitive n-th Root of Unity
result.informal_description: For any positive integer $n$, the complex exponential $e^{2\pi i/n}$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unity, meaning $(e^{2\pi i/n})^n = 1$ and $(e^{2\pi i/n})^k \neq 1$ for all $1 \leq k < n$.

name: IsPrimitiveRoot
geom_sum_isUnit'
result.signature: (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) (hj : j.Coprime n) (hj_Unit : IsUnit (j : A)) : IsUnit (∑ i ∈ range j, ζ ^ i)
result.type:
∀ {n j : ℕ} {A : Type u_1} {ζ : A} [inst : CommRing A] [IsDomain A],
  IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n → j.Coprime n → IsUnit ↑j → IsUnit (∑ i ∈ Finset.range j, ζ ^ i)
result.value:
:= by
  match n with
  | 0 => simp_all
  | 1 => simp_all
  | n + 2 => exact geom_sum_isUnit hζ (by linarith) hj
result.informal_name: Geometric Sum of Primitive Roots is a Unit
result.informal_description: Let $ A $ be a commutative ring, $ \zeta $ a primitive $ n $-th root of unity in $ A $, and $ j $ a natural number coprime to $ n $ such that $ j $ is a unit in $ A $. Then the geometric sum $ \sum_{i=0}^{j-1} \zeta^i $ is a unit in $ A $.

name: IsPrimitiveRoot
geom_sum_isUnit
result.signature: (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hj : j.Coprime n) : IsUnit (∑ i ∈ range j, ζ ^ i)
result.type:
∀ {n j : ℕ} {A : Type u_1} {ζ : A} [inst : CommRing A] [IsDomain A],
  IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n → 2 ≤ n → j.Coprime n → IsUnit (∑ i ∈ Finset.range j, ζ ^ i)
result.value:
:= by
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hζ.associated_pow_sub_one_pow_of_coprime hj (coprime_one_left n)
  convert u.isUnit
  apply mul_right_injective₀ (show 1 - ζ ≠ 0 by grind [sub_one_ne_zero])
  grind [mul_neg_geom_sum]
result.informal_name: Geometric Sum of Primitive Root is Unit for Coprime Exponent
result.informal_description: If $\zeta$ is a primitive $n$-th root of unity in a commutative monoid with $n \geq 2$ and $j$ is an integer coprime to $n$, then the geometric sum $\sum_{i=0}^{j-1} \zeta^i$ is a unit in the monoid.
